source.note: Usage reference; sample dose and contact time are editorial trials unless explicitly identified as the product’s homebrew instruction. Descriptions are newly written.

guide.how: Steep roasted nibs in finished beer using a contained addition that can be removed. Taste during extraction and record the roast level and contact time.
guide.limits: Nibs add solids and can absorb beer. A spirit tincture is an alternative extraction method; record both nib and spirit amounts separately. Roasting or soaking is not a validated sanitation step.

guide.how: Disperse unsweetened powder into a small wort slurry before a late-boil trial to reduce clumping. Compare the finished beer with a control.
guide.limits: Fat and suspended solids may change foam, texture and settling. Avoid assuming hot-chocolate mixes have the same composition as pure cocoa.

source.title: MoreBeer · oak alternatives
source.note: Usage reference; sample dose and contact time are editorial trials unless explicitly identified as the product’s homebrew instruction. Descriptions are newly written.

guide.how: Choose a toast level and oak origin, then infuse in conditioned beer. Chips extract quickly; sample frequently and remove when the balance suits the beer.
guide.limits: Use cooperage products intended for beverages. Toast and chip size change extraction; contact time is a tasting plan, not a guaranteed endpoint.

source.title: MoreBeer · oak alternatives
source.note: Usage reference; sample dose and contact time are editorial trials unless explicitly identified as the product’s homebrew instruction. Descriptions are newly written.

guide.how: Cubes offer a slower wood-contact trial than chips. Record toast, origin, dose and tasting dates so the experiment is repeatable.
guide.limits: Do not treat a small wood addition as equivalent to barrel aging. Geometry, oxygen exposure and previous use all matter.

source.title: AHA community discussion · coffee and bourbon
source.note: Usage reference; sample dose and contact time are editorial trials unless explicitly identified as the product’s homebrew instruction. Descriptions are newly written.

guide.how: Bench blend a small measured beer sample with bourbon first, then scale the preferred blend to the actual beer volume. Record the bottle strength and amount added.
guide.limits: Spirit increases both alcohol and volume; the engine currently reports the base beer only. Do not assume every bourbon is 40% ABV, and do not duplicate the same spirit as a separate tincture addition.

guide.how: Try measured bench blends before adding to the full batch. Record brand, bottle strength and whether the product is sweetened or spiced.
guide.limits: Alcohol, dilution and any sugar are not included in the base-beer numbers. This is an editorial alternative to bourbon, not a sourced universal dose.

source.title: MoreBeer · vanilla beans
source.note: Usage reference; sample dose and contact time are editorial trials unless explicitly identified as the product’s homebrew instruction. Descriptions are newly written.

guide.how: Split a bean and contain it for a short conditioned-beer extraction trial. A measured tincture lets you compare several blend levels before committing the batch.
guide.limits: Bean size and quality vary; count is not a fixed mass. Vanilla-like sweetness is a sensory association, not measured residual sugar.

source.note: Usage reference; sample dose and contact time are editorial trials unless explicitly identified as the product’s homebrew instruction. Descriptions are newly written.

guide.how: Select a food-grade extract and use measured bench trials. Enter your chosen amount after checking the actual concentration.
guide.limits: No generic dose is prefilled. Extracts differ in strength, alcohol, sugar and flavor composition; the reference describes vanilla beans rather than verifying a particular extract.

guide.how: Use a contained coarse-coffee trial in conditioned beer and sample early. Record coffee origin, roast, grind and contact time.
guide.limits: Grounds can absorb beer and create sediment. Roast and extraction conditions may push the flavor toward bitterness or acidity; these effects are not predicted.

guide.how: Bench blend prepared coffee into measured beer samples. Scale the chosen ratio to the actual packaging volume.
guide.limits: Strength varies widely; the trial amount is an editorial example. Added water, coffee extract and any sweeteners are not modeled.

guide.how: Use unsweetened coconut in a contained conditioned-beer trial. Record toast level and sample over several days.
guide.limits: Fat can affect foam and shelf character; coconut also absorbs liquid. The app does not model oil extraction or volume loss.

guide.how: Begin with a small weighed late-boil trial or compare a measured tincture after fermentation. Record the spice form because sticks and powder extract differently.
guide.limits: The dose is an editorial trial, not a universal recommendation. Large spice loads can dominate a beer; extraction and perceived heat are not modeled.

guide.how: Crush shortly before a late-boil addition and record the seed source. Useful as a small citrus-spice trial in wheat or Belgian-style beers.
guide.limits: Freshness and variety affect aroma. This starting amount is a house suggestion; the source is a general supplier category.

guide.how: Record whether the peel is bitter or sweet and add near the end of the boil for an initial trial. Keep the variety consistent when comparing batches.
guide.limits: Pith and processing change bitterness. IBU from peel and its aroma extraction are outside the hop-based engine.

guide.how: Prepare a small weighed amount for a late-boil trial. Record peeling, cut size and contact time to make comparisons useful.
guide.limits: Fresh ginger varies in pungency. This is an editorial experimental starting point, not a standardized ingredient potency.

guide.how: Choose a known pepper and bench-test a small infusion before a full batch addition. Record variety, seeds, preparation and the amount actually used.
guide.limits: No generic dose is prefilled because pepper potency varies greatly. Perceived heat is not represented by IBU or by this flavor model.

source.title: MoreBeer · fruit in beer
source.note: Usage reference; sample dose and contact time are editorial trials unless explicitly identified as the product’s homebrew instruction. Descriptions are newly written.

guide.how: Use a brewing-suitable purée during or after primary fermentation, following its supplier instructions. Provide space for renewed fermentation and track gravity.
guide.limits: Fruit sugars can restart fermentation. Confirm completion before packaging; extract, acidity, color, alcohol and fruit-related losses are not included in predictions.

guide.how: Record the fruit variety and use a brewing-suitable purée. Allow renewed fermentation to complete before evaluating a final blend.
guide.limits: Sweetened products differ from unsweetened purée. Fruit fermentability and acidity are not inferred from the entered mass.

source.title: MoreBeer · fruit in beer
source.note: Usage reference; sample dose and contact time are editorial trials unless explicitly identified as the product’s homebrew instruction. Descriptions are newly written.

guide.how: Introduce a brewing-suitable purée during or after primary and track the renewed fermentation. Record the purée product and any dilution.
guide.limits: The mass is a house trial suggestion. Pectin, fruit sugar and retained solids can affect haze, gravity and yield; the engine does not calculate them.

guide.how: A kettle fining used to help wort proteins settle. Check your supplier dose and hydration instructions, then add late in the boil.
guide.limits: Dose is left at zero until set from your product label; teaspoon mass varies. Clarity depends on the whole process, and no fixed clarity or flavor improvement is promised.

guide.how: A convenient tablet-form kettle fining for late-boil use. Enter a dose appropriate to the specific tablet and batch volume.
guide.limits: Tablet sizes and dose directions vary. This row is not a second required addition alongside Irish moss; avoid unintentionally doubling the same fining role.

guide.how: A post-fermentation clarification option. Follow product preparation directions, then allow settling under the intended conditioning conditions.
guide.limits: Gelatin is animal-derived. Dose and preparation are product-specific, so no universal amount is prefilled. Clarification can change presentation and suspended material; it is not a numerical flavor adjustment.

guide.limits: Biofine Clear is a product example, not a concentration shared by all silica preparations. No universal dose or guaranteed settling time is assumed.

source.title: Wyeast · Beer Nutrient Blend
source.note: Usage reference; sample dose and contact time are editorial trials unless explicitly identified as the product’s homebrew instruction. Descriptions are newly written.

guide.how: This specific homebrew product lists 2.2 g per 19 L and a kettle addition 10–15 minutes before the boil ends. The prefill scales that homebrew instruction to 20 L.
guide.limits: The manufacturer separately lists a professional rate; this entry deliberately uses the homebrew directions. Other nutrient products are not interchangeable by mass. Nutrient addition does not automatically raise the model’s attenuation.
